title: Normalized left refinement on a fixed pair of transported operations
statement: Fix l, Omega, D, X,Y,f and compactifications c,d as in the refinement data, and let r:c to d be a proper refinement. For arbitrary Transport records A on c and B on d, including the actual normalized integral scalar maps and the prescribed closed action on common-stage transitions, there exists LeftMates A B r: at each stage an isomorphism alpha:A.F to B.F commuting with integer shifts, with the open-unit proper/open ring normalization and the rational and common-field left conjugation formulas. This supplies no right comparison, adjunction equations, or strict-system realization package.

proof.text: At $A=A_{E,n}$ take the given exact finite adjunctions for $c,d$. Let $e_u:j_{d!}\to Ru_*j_{c!}$ be the proper/open comparison. Compactification coherence gives an invertible natural map $C_u:F_A^d\to F_A^c$ by $Rp_{d,*}(e_u)$ and the direct-image compositor. Set $\alpha_{u,A}=C_u^{-1}$. This restricts to the actual full finite-Tor categories since both endpoint functors take values there. The refinement coefficient/site lemma identifies the etale and pro-etale $e_u$ by their open-adjunction transposes, including the clopen-section restriction, rather than by an arbitrary isomorphism. Consequently this $\alpha$ has precisely the stated open-unit normalization. The hypotheses are finite coefficients, bounded constructible input, proper $u$, and $uj_c=j_d$; none requires absolute separatedness or a Cartesian refinement square.

proof.text: On the strict semilinear systems put $\mathsf F^a=S_{p_a}J_{j_a}$ for $a=c,d$ and form $\mathsf C_u=c_{p_d,u}J_{j_c}\circ S_{p_d}\Gamma_{Q_u}:\mathsf F^d\to\mathsf F^c$, with $Q_u=(j_c,j_d,1_X,u)$. The system realization theorem constructs this map intrinsically, before evaluation, and identifies its evaluated maps with the normalized finite comparisons of step 1. On $\mathcal R_XK$ the input and both endpoints are normalized, have etale-origin constructible levels, and common cohomological/Tor bounds by integral reconstruction and system transport. Apply finite operations also to the open/proper intermediate morphisms, with their own compactifications, and take the larger of the finitely many common bounds. Since exact evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms, $\mathsf C_u$ is invertible on this domain. Define $\mathsf\alpha_u=\mathsf C_u^{-1}$. Only invertibility, never equality of maps, was detected by evaluations.

proof.text:
Transport $\mathcal L_Y(\mathsf\alpha_u\mathcal R_X)$ through the specified identifications $F^a_R\cong\mathcal L_Y\mathsf F^a\mathcal R_X$ to define $\alpha_{u,R}$. Integral reconstruction supplies exactly those identifications and the prescribed $r_{a,R}$. The system-realization theorem intertwines $\Gamma_{Q_u}$ and direct-image composition with their ambient proper/open maps. It therefore gives, as an equality of actual integral transformations,
$$r_{d,R}\,I_Y(\alpha_{u,R})=(C_u^{\rm amb})^{-1}\,r_{c,R}.$$
Here $C_u^{\rm amb}$ is ambient proper composition after $Rp_{d,*}e_u$. Inversion and naturality preserve the intertwining equality. Its input system equality is the intrinsic proper/open word of step 2, not a family selected from finite components. This proves the integral normalization with the same compact-support representatives.

proof.text: The proper/open word commutes with shifts: its open base-change and clopen projection constituents do so on simultaneous complex models, and the direct-image shift is the adjoint of the termwise inverse-image shift. Units and counits commute with these adjoint shifts; writing a mate as unit, whiskered map and counit therefore preserves its shift square. The direct-image compositor is the conjugate of pullback composition, so the same argument applies to it. Composition, whiskering and inversion preserve shift compatibility. The constant ring sequence $C_m=A$ and evaluation give this argument at each finite coefficient; the diagram shift model imposes no normalization or constructibility assumption. For the integral maps, slotwise realization shift coherence identifies these same system shifts with the prescribed termwise/Roos-cone shifts under $r_{c,R},r_{d,R}$. Thus both left maps already constructed have the shifts required in the statement.

proof.text: Whisker the whole-system proper/open scalar square by the proper image. Its proper composition identity gives the left refinement scalar square before total limit. Transport.scalarIntegralNormalized identifies the scalar maps with those exact whole-system maps; Transport.scalarRationalNormalized fixes their localizations. proof.text: Localize the normalized integral left refinement and its inverse on the same objects and Hom modules. For a rational arrow h divided by a power of a uniformizer, integral naturality multiplied by the inverse denominator gives rational naturality; finite sums follow by additivity. The given Transport.localizationNormalized identifies this localized map with the conjugation through the fixed q maps. Shift compatibility and the integral scalar-enlargement equation localize as equalities of the same maps. This proves the required rationalLeft formula, without constructing any right map.

proof.text: On a closed-stage object represented by (E,K), define the left refinement component by q of B composed with the image of the rational refinement and inverse q of A. A common-stage arrow is represented over a larger finite field M. The normalized scalar comparison from the preceding steps identifies enlargement of both rational refinements, and Transport.commonTransitionNormalized fixes the action of both closed functors on the transition arrows. Thus rational naturality over M gives closed naturality independently of M. Applying this to the inverse transformations gives inverse closed components. The prescribed common shifts and rational shifts give the closed shift square; the formula on each common inclusion is the stated commonLeft equality. No right functor or adjunction equation is asserted in this step.

proof.text: Use Transport.commonTransitionNormalized to compute both closed left functors on transitions between fields, through their prescribed rational realizations. The normalized integral scalar maps and their rational localization, together with the proper/open scalar square, make the rational refinement commute with these transition actions. Every common-field arrow is represented by a stage arrow and transition isomorphisms, so their common components give a natural isomorphism on all arrows. This is why per-field q identities alone would not suffice.
